subject: compostable cups for soup?
body:
Hi UNIQ team!

We're switching our restaurant to eco-friendly packaging. Can we use your 12oz compostable cups for our hot soups? They go out at about 165°F. Also, can our customers toss them in their home compost bin?

Thanks so much,
Sofia
Greenleaf Kitchen
needs_human_reason: Both questions are answered directly by the KB product facts (PLA rated to 110°F; commercially compostable only). No hot-food container is suggested because the KB doesn't list one.
summary: Restaurant asks whether 12 oz compostable cups work for 165°F soup and for home compost. No to both (110°F max, commercial compost only).
draft_reply:
Hi Sofia,

Unfortunately our 12 oz compostable cups won't work for hot soup, and they aren't home compostable. The PLA lining is rated up to 110°F (43°C), so 165°F soup is too hot for them, and they're commercially compostable only, meaning they need an industrial composting facility rather than a backyard bin.

They're a great fit for ice cream, frozen yogurt, and other cold foods. Our kraft hot cups are rated for hot drinks up to 190°F, but we don't list a container rated for hot food like soup, so we'd rather not guess on that one.

Love that you're making the switch to eco-friendly packaging!

The UNIQ Supply Team
